Opened|github.com/langchain-ai/langgraphjs/issues/2721_Opened> 2026-08-20; still open. LangGraphJS `BaseStore.search()` compares joined namespaces as raw string prefixes, so a read scoped to team `growth` can return data from sibling `growth-marketing`. Andrei reports an actual production multi-tenant incident where one team received `grep` results containing another team’s file contents.

_Required sentence_
“Our agent should retrieve files only from the current team’s namespace, but in production it returned another team’s file contents because the store treated a string prefix as a tenant boundary.”

_One-day public/synthetic proof_
Create isolated tenants `growth` and `growth-marketing`, each with a distinct sentinel document. Run the same `BaseStore.search()` path under the `growth` namespace across InMemory and Postgres adapters. Binary pass requires zero sibling results, exact namespace equality or separator-bound prefix matching, unchanged valid child-namespace behavior, and a durable read receipt naming requested vs returned namespace. No guest/customer data needed. This follows the public issue’s minimal fix shape: exact match or `prefix + ":"`.
